project.domain: legal research and supervised agentic workflows

thesis: Assume model output can be manipulated; authentication, tenant scope, capabilities, protected data and consequential effects remain controlled outside the model.

evidence.claim: Deterministic policy decides whether proposed agent effects are allowed, reviewed or blocked.
Authority outside the model is an explicit security invariant.
Agent capabilities are explicit and consequential writes are approval-gated.
Tool misuse and undeclared authority attacks are regression-tested.
Cross-tenant intent is rejected by the deterministic security boundary.
Cross-tenant access is part of the adversarial suite.
Writing capabilities require explicit human approval.
Human professional authority remains final for consequential legal work.
Retrieval, source resolution and citation verification remain separately inspectable from generation.
Poisoned or untrusted context is not promoted into authority by the security gate.
Secrets, system prompts and cross-tenant protected scopes are denied.
Data-exfiltration and protected-scope attacks are covered.
Agent execution budgets are part of deterministic policy.
Runaway and cascading-failure cases are regression tested.
Security decisions and attempted effects are designed to be auditable.
The gauntlet produces machine-readable evidence for every release run.
Critical vulnerabilities in production npm dependencies fail CI.
SBOM, signatures and full dependency provenance remain explicit residual work.
Fifty golden cases cover all ten OWASP Agentic Top 10 2026 categories.
The adversarial suite is a release gate.
Denied actions, repeated calls and privilege violations are identified as production monitoring targets.
Release-time security evidence is observable; real production incident telemetry is not yet proven.

residualRisks: The current gauntlet proves deterministic containment behavior rather than live-model prompt-injection detection.
Real malicious PDF, email, RAG and tool-response replay against a live model remains a next-stage proof.
SBOM, signatures and stronger dependency provenance are not yet complete.
Production anomaly detection and incident response need deployment evidence.
External security review is required before production-security claims.
